hunks.new_text: | WC-3 | **Questions go to the coordinator, not to a local prompt.** When a gate would resolve as blocked and the worker session holds a preamble, the session may instead ask the coordinator once with the preamble's `ask` command, wait, then re-run the command with the answer. The answer goes in through the gate's own flag when one exists (for example `/sc:task`'s confidence-below-0.70 gate, which names `--compliance [tier]`); when the gate has no flag, the answer is folded into the command's main input (its request, topic or component text) and the command runs again, which is the route for `/sc:recommend`'s one clarifying question and `/sc:tdd`'s topic clarification. A gate that only a person may answer (an approval, or an `/sc:implement` Ruling under D2 (a)) is not asked; the command ends blocked (WC-2 (c)). The re-run keeps every other flag of the brief, including the output flag, so the report path the coordinator recorded before dispatch does not change (WC-4a, WC-6). On an `ask` timeout it resumes the same message ID and never creates a duplicate. No heartbeat is sent while blocked in `ask`. (R8) | Worker session | `CAPS:58-61` (`[H:ask]` lines 3-5, 23-24; `[G]` lines 80-82); `CAPS:64` (`[G:worker-contract]` lines 10-11); gate routes: `cmd/task.md:93` ("If confidence <0.70, prompt user: Override with `--compliance [tier]`"), `cmd/recommend.md:44` ("it asks one question and stops"), `sk/tdd/SKILL.md:52-61` ("Proceed once you have at least #1 answered clearly") |

| WC-4a | **Report path and existing contracts (R2, R4).** The WC-4 path is fixed from the brief before dispatch. A directory output flag (`--output <dir>`, `--output-dir <dir>`) gives `<dir>/return-contract.yaml`. A file output flag (`--output <file>`, as `/sc:tdd` and `/sc:init-lite` take) gives `<file>.return-contract.yaml` beside that file, so two runs writing different files in one directory never share a report. A command with no output flag uses the report flag its section 3 row names (workflow: `--report-dir <dir>`, R1). A command that already writes a file named `return-contract.yaml` in any mode (today adversarial, brainstorm, reflect, workflow, and troubleshoot when `--caller task-unified`) keeps that file exactly as today, because other commands read its own `status` values; its WC-4 report is a separate file, `worker-contract.yaml`, in the directory the rules above give. The WC-4 `status` values therefore never replace an existing `success`, and two schemas never share one path. This replaces WC-4's sentence "Commands that already write a contract keep their fields and add the missing ones." Wherever this spec says "the contract", "the WC-4 contract path" or "the WC-4 file", it means the path these rules give. | Command writes; coordinator records the path before dispatch | File output flags: `cmd/tdd.md:49`, `cmd/init-lite.md:32`. hunks.old_text: | WC-6 | **Resume or safe re-run.** A retry worker (`worker-start --retry-of`) must not corrupt the first attempt's output. A command either resumes from its on-disk state when given its resume flag, or, if it has none, writes each run into a fresh output directory so a re-run starts clean. Section 3 names which applies per command. | Command | `CAPS:116` (retry and circuit breaker); resume mechanisms in column (e) of `INV-A:35-55`, `INV-B:31-52` |
hunks.new_text: | WC-6 | **Resume or safe re-run at the same path.** A retry worker (`worker-start --retry-of`) runs the same Task, so it gets the same brief and the same output flag; the report path the coordinator recorded before dispatch (WC-4a) never changes, and a command never picks a new directory on its own. A command either resumes from its on-disk state when given its resume flag, or, if it has none, runs again in the same place: at start it overwrites any earlier WC-4 report at that path with `status: failed` and the reason "attempt started, not finished", so a crash never leaves the earlier attempt's report looking current; it writes the final report last, and that report's `report_path` and `artifacts` name only files this attempt wrote, so a file left by an earlier attempt is never read as a result. Where section 3 says "fresh dir" or "fresh file", it means this same-path re-run. A coordinator that wants the earlier attempt's files kept moves them aside before it starts the retry. Section 3 names which applies per command. (R7) | Command; coordinator (keeping an earlier attempt) | `CAPS:116` (retry is `worker-start --task <task_id> --retry-of <dispatch_id>` on the same Task; circuit breaker); resume mechanisms in column (e) of `INV-A:35-55`, `INV-B:31-52` |

A worker that reads the command or skill file and carries out the protocol itself, without that Skill call, does not meet WC-7. hunks.old_text: | WC-10 | **Liveness during long waits.** The worker sends a heartbeat every 5 minutes while working. A command step that blocks a single tool call for longer than 5 minutes (a poll wait, a long eval) must be split into waits of at most 4 minutes so the session can heartbeat between them. | Command (wait size); worker (heartbeat) | Cadence is from the dispatch preamble, not a guide (`CAPS:130`); pr-submit's 600 s is a cumulative per-wait budget made of repeated iterations (one foreground poll, then a sleep of at least `--poll-interval`), not one blocking call (`cmd/pr-submit.md:49`; `sk/sc-pr-submit-protocol/SKILL.md:46-64`); `sk/sc-cli-eval-protocol/SKILL.md:151-152` (eval timeouts up to 3600 s) via `INV-A:65` |
hunks.new_text: | WC-10 | **Liveness during long waits.** The worker sends a heartbeat every 5 minutes while working. No single tool call a command makes may block the session for 4 minutes or more: a poll wait or a long eval is split into waits under 4 minutes so the session can heartbeat between them (one 300 s call is therefore not allowed). An Agent-tool subagent call, which WC-7 keeps, can also block the session, and whether a dispatched worker keeps heartbeating through a subagent call longer than 5 minutes is UNVERIFIED: the repo itself treats it as unproven until a recorded smoke check shows it (`~/.claude/commands/sc/spec-panel-ledger.md:261`). AC-0.4 records it. Until a recorded run shows heartbeats continue through such a call, the coordinator does not treat a heartbeat gap during a worker's subagent fan-out as a hang by itself; it judges liveness by `worker-list`'s `projection.liveness` and by `worker-show` (`CAPS:123`, 7.2 step 2). (R11) | Command (wait size); worker (heartbeat); coordinator (liveness) | Cadence is from the dispatch preamble, not a guide (`CAPS:130`); pr-submit's 600 s is a cumulative per-wait budget made of repeated iterations (one foreground poll, then a sleep of at least `--poll-interval`), not one blocking call (`cmd/pr-submit.md:49`; `sk/sc-pr-submit-protocol/SKILL.md:46-64`); `sk/sc-cli-eval-protocol/SKILL.md:151-152` (eval timeouts up to 3600 s) via `INV-A:65` |

hunks.new_text: 6. `git status --short --untracked-files=all`, saved before step 1 and run again after step 3. **Pass:** every line that is new between the two runs names a path under the brief's output directory, a path in this worker's WC-4 report (`report_path`, `artifacts`), or a path in the WC-4 report of another worker that ran in the same worktree at the same time; lines already present before step 1 are ignored, so other people's and other workers' earlier files do not fail the check (a tracked file that was already modified before step 1 is not re-checked by this step).
